---
title: HTML Math
---

## Overview

Math in Quarto documents is written in LaTeX syntax, inline between `$…$`
and as display math between `$$…$$`. For HTML output the
`html-math-method` option chooses how the browser renders it:

``` yaml
format:
  html:
    html-math-method: mathjax
```

| Method    | How the math is rendered                                                   |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `mathjax` | MathJax typesets the TeX in the browser (the default).                     |
| `katex`   | KaTeX typesets the TeX in the browser.                                     |
| `mathml`  | Quarto converts the TeX to MathML when it renders; no JavaScript is loaded.|
| `plain`   | The TeX is left as written, with no renderer.                              |

`mathjax` and `katex` also accept an object form to point at your own copy
of the library:

``` yaml
format:
  html:
    html-math-method:
      method: katex
      url: https://example.org/katex/
```

## Native MathML

With `html-math-method: mathml`, every expression is converted to
[MathML Core](https://www.w3.org/TR/mathml-core/) at render time and
written into the page as a `<math>` element. Every current browser
renders MathML Core natively, so the page loads no math library and the
math is part of the document rather than something a script draws after
the page loads. The converted element also carries the original TeX in an
annotation, so copying an equation still gives you its source.

A few things to know:

- **Fallback.** If an expression uses a command the converter does not
  know, that expression is left as TeX and MathJax is loaded for the
  page so it still renders. Quarto reports a `Q-22-*` warning that points
  at the command in your `.qmd`; fixing it (or defining the macro in the
  expression with `\newcommand`) removes the dependency on MathJax. See
  [Q-22-1](../../../errors/math/Q-22-1.qmd) for the most common case.
- **Equation numbers.** Numbered equations (`$$…$$ {#eq-name}`) show
  their number as a label to the right of the equation, outside the math.
- **Fonts.** Browsers lay out MathML with a math font when one is
  installed (Windows ships Cambria Math; Firefox bundles STIX). Without
  one, the browser falls back to the page font and some constructs, such
  as large operators and stretchy delimiters, look less refined than with
  MathJax or KaTeX. Quarto does not ship a math font.
- **`\cancel`.** The strike-through is drawn by Firefox but not by
  Chrome, which shows the content without the line.

## Unsupported methods

Quarto 1's `webtex` and `gladtex` methods are not available. They are
treated like `plain`: the TeX stays in the page unrendered.
